title: Gradual Unwind Rollback Drill & Ops Cheat Sheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick-reference drill and procedural checklist for rehearsing a gradual unwind (soft rollback / rollforward-to-safe-config) during high-risk launches. Intentionally compact so on-call and runbook leads can run a rehearsal in under 45 minutes and iterate after each drill.

Scope:
- Applies to any staged rollout that supports traffic slices (canary by user-hash, region, or product lane).
- Focused on gradual unwind (reduce exposure, switch to compat variant, then full rollback if needed).
- Includes preflight, unwind steps, verification, communications, and post-drill retrospective prompts.

Preflight (T-72 to T-0 checklist):
- Confirm saved baseline: snapshot config, model version, routing rules (S3/GCS path + git tag).
- Deploy telemetry hooks: ensure metric tags for rollout_id and cohort present.
- Prepare quick-fallback artifacts: image tags, model artifact ids, config-override files.
- Validate smoke endpoints: run smoke suite against staging and canary, record response latencies.
- Notify watchers: rotation leads, SRE, on-call, product owner. Post link to #release-ops.
- Kill-switch sanity: verify API that can cut traffic to hosted-fallback is functional from two regions.

Trigger thresholds (example values — tune per product):
- Error rate delta: > 1.5x baseline sustained for 3 minutes (5m rolling)
- Latency p95: > baseline + 200ms sustained for 5 minutes
- Token-cost regression: > 12% increase token/sec (economics guardrail)
- QA regression: eval set fail rate increase > 8%
- Observability spike: unexplained memory / GPU OOMs or KV cache thrash

Gradual Unwind Flow (fast path):
1) Canary pause: immediately pause new cohort promotions.
2) Cohort shrink (30 min window): reduce canary weight to 0.5x current and hold for 10 minutes. Observe telemetry.
3) Route to compat model: if issue persists, switch cohort to compatible model-variant (quantized / lower context) using routing policy.
4) Prefix cache clear (selective): clear KV cache for affected cohort if corruption suspected.
5) Full rollback: if persistent failures or safety breaches, execute full rollback to previous model + config.
6) Post-rollback validation: run synthetic suite and targeted sample checks on impacted accounts.

Rollback Drill Script (run in rehearsal):
- T+00:00 (Start) - Lead: Release Engineer. Announce drill in #release-ops with drill-id and expected timeline.
- T+00:03 - Trigger simulated error via canary fault-inject endpoint (test-only). Verify alert fires.
- T+00:06 - Execute 'canary pause' and note alert behavior.
- T+00:12 - Shrink cohort to 25% of prior weight. Annotate metrics.
- T+00:20 - Route cohort to compat model-variant. Verify success responses.
- T+00:28 - If still failing, perform full rollback to previous stable tag.
- T+00:35 - Run post-rollback validation: smoke + 30 sampled user requests.
- T+00:42 - Declare drill complete and capture key timestamps in ticket.

Verification checklist (post-action):
- Check: all user traffic is served by expected model versions (list versions in ticket).
- Check: alerts cleared and no new regressions for 30 minutes.
- Check: telemetry tags show rollout_id drained.
- Run: sample QA prompts (10) and capture outputs. Save diffs to artifact storage.
- Run: token-cost smoke to ensure no unexpected increase.

Telemetry sampling plan (practical):
- High-priority metrics: error_rate, p95_latency, model_version, cohort_id, gpu_util, kv_cache_hit_ratio.
- Sampling windows: 1m for alerting; 5m/30m for trend analysis.
- Include synthetic probes every 30s from 3 regions for canary cohorts.
- Maintain a short trace (trace id) for first 50 failing requests for forensic.

72-hour rehearsal mini-calendar (example timeline for drill run and follow-up):
- Day 0: Run drill (assign roles, execute script, collect artifacts).
- Day 0 + 2 hours: Quick sync (15m) to capture immediate findings.
- Day 1: Engineering triage session (60m) update tickets with actions.
- Day 2: Run expanded smoke with expanded sample set (50 requests).
- Day 3: Publish brief retrospective + checklist updates.

Roles & RACI (compact):
- Release lead (R): coordinate drill, timeline, exec summary.
- SRE on-call (A): execute traffic shifts, throttle policies, confirm infrastructure health.
- Serving engineer (C): perform config switches, rollback commands, model pinning.
- QA (C): run sample validation set and report diffs.
- Product owner (I): informed of drill outcome and user impact estimate.

Communication templates (short):
- Initial shout: "Drill: unwinding rollout-id {RID} starting now. Expect ~45m. Watch #release-ops."
- Alert escalation: "ALERT: {metric} breached for {RID}. Taking step: {action}. Owner: {person}."
- Post-rollback status: "Action: rolled back to {tag}. Validation: smoke OK (Y/N). Next steps: {notes}."

Common failure modes & mitigations (notes):
- Slow warmup when switching variants -> mitigate with staged warm-warm cohorts and prefetch cache populate.
- Telemetry tag missing -> enforce rollout_id injection at gateway layer.
- Compatibility mismatch -> keep compatibility matrix in repo and add contract tests.

Post-drill retro prompts (capture in ticket):
- What worked? (short bullets)
- What surprised us?
- What should be automated before next drill?
- Update runbook sections (exact commands, file paths, links).
- Owners for follow-ups + deadlines.

Command snippets (placeholders) - copy into ops binder:
- shrink cohort: curl -X POST https://deploy-api/release/adjust-weight -d "{\"rid\": \"RID\", \"weight\": 0.25}"
- switch variant: ./deployctl route --rid RID --cohort A --to model-v1-compat
- rollback: ./deployctl rollback --rid RID --to-tag v2026-09-02-stable

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical 'compat' model naming convention and add to model-catalog. (Owner: Priya)
- Can we automate selective KV cache clears per cohort? (Owner: Diego)
- Add a lightweight synthetic generator producing prompt families for quick validation (Owner: Noah)

References & artifacts:
- Ticket template: REL-DRILL-TEMPLATE.md (repo: infra/runbooks)
- Canary routing docs: confluence/deploys/canary-routing
- Observability playbook: SRE/telemetry/alerting-baselines

Notes to self:
- Keep drill short and deterministic: reduce "what if" branches.
- Capture exact timings for each action (UTC) to feed into postmortem timelines.
- Next drill: include business continuity rep to weigh user-facing comms cadence.

-- end --
